The morning light falls across the quiet wooden table today
A cup of tea steams beside an open blank notebook
Outside a bird repeats one small bright persistent question now
I think about doors that close without making any sound
Dust floats in the air like slow forgotten tiny stars
Somewhere a train carries strangers toward their ordinary evenings again
A window reflects my face and then the passing cloud
I remember a promise I never meant to keep fully
The clock taps forward as if it knows something important
There is no reason to hurry but I hurry anyway
The street below is wet from rain I missed earlier
A child laughs somewhere and the sound feels like proof
Maybe we are all just waiting to be noticed kindly
I write a word then cross it out gently again
The page accepts everything and asks for nothing in return
A shadow moves across the floor like a shy visitor
I wonder whether silence is a kind of answer too
The tea cools while my thoughts keep warming themselves today
A memory of summer arrives uninvited and sits down near
I let it stay because even old light can comfort
Once I believed every day had to contain a revelation
Now I look for small mercies hidden in plain sight
A sock under the bed may be a tiny tragedy
The kettle sings and the kitchen becomes briefly holy again
I think about all the versions of me that left
They stand in hallways I can visit only while dreaming
One of them waves and I wave back slowly too
We never speak but maybe that is the kindest language
Outside the wind rearranges leaves into temporary maps of nowhere
I watch them and feel oddly faithful to the world
A phone screen brightens then darkens without offering any news
Perhaps nothing happening is also a quiet kind of gift
The chair creaks and I forgive it for being old
I should water the plant but I forget once more
Its leaves are patient and still green enough to hope
There is courage in continuing to grow toward a window
I envy the way simple things commit to being simple
Yet humans are allowed to be complicated on purpose sometimes
I open the drawer and find batteries old photographs coins
Each object is a sentence I can no longer read
The afternoon stretches out like a road without traffic today
I could leave but leaving requires shoes and reasons too
So I stay and count the sounds around me carefully
A refrigerator hums a note that never resolves anywhere completely
A door closes upstairs and the house settles again softly
My breath becomes a small tide I can follow inward
In and out the world makes its earliest proposal again
I accept without signing anything and that seems sufficient today
Perhaps being alive is mostly noticing what remains nearby always
The spoon in the sink shines with unimportant glory anyway
I think of someone I loved and lost gently once
Their face arrives not as a picture but as weather
It rains in me and I do not open umbrellas
Some feelings deserve to be wet before they dry completely
I remember a kitchen where bread rose slowly overnight once
The smell was so patient it felt like family then
We ate with our hands and called it enough always
Now enough is a word I practice every day slowly
The sky turns a color no one can own entirely
I try to keep it by not keeping it forever
A dog barks at nothing and then seems satisfied again
Maybe nothing was always there and needed naming by us
We invented friendly ghosts to keep the corners company tonight
I am not afraid of dark empty spaces anymore now
They hold room for things too large for ordinary daylight
A clock ticks and the seconds become tiny bricks slowly
I build a house from waiting and call it mine
Inside there are chairs for regret and hope placed equally
They sit facing each other and rarely speak first nowadays
I serve them tea and pretend I am fair always
The evening arrives wearing blue and smelling faintly of rain
I let it enter because I am tired of locks
The old lock was never keeping anything safe anyway now
Sometimes safety is just another quiet name for distance now
I choose closeness even when it costs me my certainty
A streetlamp flickers like it has something to confess tonight
I confess too but only to the listening air outside
It receives my words without becoming any heavier at all
Maybe confession is just breath returning to where it began
Maybe beginning is simply remembering we were never truly alone
The night deepens and the room becomes more honest now
Objects stop performing and let themselves be merely things again
My hands rest in my lap like small sleeping animals
I let them be and do not ask questions anymore
Somewhere an ambulance passes carrying urgency through ordinary streets tonight
I hope someone is saved and then I hope gently
Hope is not always loud sometimes it is humming softly
A small moth circles the lamp with terrible devotion tonight
I understand wanting something so much it becomes direction itself
Still I turn the lamp lower and give quiet mercy
The words are almost finished and I feel oddly calm
As if talking to nothing had practiced being something real
I do not know where these sentences came from exactly
I only know they arrived when I stopped blocking them
Maybe writing is opening a window inside the mind slowly
Maybe reading is letting weather enter another person quietly now
Outside a late car passes and then silence returns gently
I place the pen down and listen to the room
The room is full of everything that did not happen
I give thanks for that too and close my eyes
